theme: Graphite GPU backend and new platforms
highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.151.1 adds the new Graphite GPU backend for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn, plus Nano Server font support.
highlights_body: The new SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET package and Graphite bindings bring the next-generation Skia GPU engine to .NET consumers. Nano Server gains font rendering via FreeType, async pixel read-back lands for SKImage and SKSurface, and several hot allocation paths are eliminated.

bullets.lead: Graphite GPU backend: Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn
bullets.detail: The new Skia Graphite rendering engine is now exposed via managed bindings. A dedicated SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET package ships Vulkan support, with Metal and Dawn accessible through the same Graphite API surface.
Additional upstream chrome/m151 bug fixes and a Skia submodule/cgmanifest sync to pick up the latest stability improvements.

bullets.lead: Async RequestReadPixels on SKImage and SKSurface
bullets.detail: New backend-neutral async pixel read-back allows reading pixels from GPU-backed images and surfaces without stalling the GPU pipeline.

bullets.lead: Binding generation made deterministic across platforms
bullets.detail: The native binding generator now produces identical output regardless of the host OS, eliminating spurious diffs when regenerating on different platforms.
SKData.SaveTo avoids a double buffer copy on the hot save path, and SKRuntimeEffectUniforms pre-sizes its internal uniform lookup map to the known count, removing repeated resizing.
The null-terminated code path in GetEncodedText no longer allocates an intermediate string, reducing allocations in text measurement loops.

bullets.lead: CoTaskMem pixel-buffer leak in SKImage.Create fixed
bullets.detail: The raster failure path in SKImage.Create leaked a CoTaskMem-allocated pixel buffer when the native image creation failed. The buffer is now always freed.

bullets.lead: Nano Server font support via FreeType
bullets.detail: SkiaSharp now uses FreeType for font rendering on Nano Server, where GDI is unavailable, enabling text drawing in Windows Server Core and Nano Server container workloads.

bullets.lead: Containerized test legs: Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, Nano Server
bullets.detail: CI now runs tests inside Azure Linux, Alpine (musl libc), and Nano Server containers, validating native library compatibility across lightweight and minimal Linux/Windows environments.

bullets.lead: Windows: MSVC environment initialized once per native build
bullets.detail: The MSVC toolchain environment is now set up once at the start of a native build rather than per-step, improving build reliability and speed on Windows.
